## Teaching points

1. Elevated ketones with low or normal glucose after alcohol use and poor intake suggest alcoholic ketoacidosis. Give thiamine and carbohydrate-containing fluids, monitor electrolytes and consider other causes of acidosis.
2. Thiamine, carbohydrate-containing fluids, electrolyte replacement and reassessment are central; exclude competing causes of acidosis.
3. Dextrose-containing IV fluids are absent from the catalog. This case cannot simulate full biochemical correction; do not substitute thiamine alone or automatically make ketones normalize.
